sentences.text: In a wide field, a breeze lifted a red kite above the grass.
The flyer let out string, and the kite climbed in small tugs.
Then the wind shifted. The kite dove toward a fence, and the string went slack.
A slack string is a loose string, and a loose string cannot steer.
The flyer did not yank. A hard yank can snap the string or crash the kite.
Instead, the flyer took a few steps forward until the string grew tight again.
A gentle pull lifted the nose of the kite.
The kite shuddered, caught the breeze, and rose over the fence.
After that, the flyer kept one hand ready to give string and one hand ready to take it in.
Giving string lets a kite go higher. Taking string in can steady it.
By the end of the hour, the flyer could feel the difference between a useful pull and a panicked one.
The kite landed on purpose, not in the fence, and the red cloth was still in one piece.
